Jonas / team —

Drafted answers below for Lisa's three bullets. I included concise evidence references and an ask for any environment-specific constraints we should note. Please review and flag edits. I'll prepare the row-by-row spreadsheet once we confirm wording.

--- Draft answers ---
1) Audit logs access: For Private (VPC) and Dedicated customers we provide streaming / near-real-time access to audit logs via a secure log-forwarder (TLS to the customer-owned SIEM) and also support scheduled exports (S3 exports). For Hosted customers, full audit logs are retained and available via secure export; real-time streaming is available on request as part of a Dedicated offer. (See Appendix §3.1, Evidence: sample-logs.tar.gz, logging-architecture-diagram.pdf)

2) Cross-tenant memory/KV separation: The serving runtime enforces logical tenant isolation at the process and memory allocation layers. For Dedicated pools, customers get isolated GPU allocation and per-tenant process sandboxes; KV cache namespaces are namespaced per-tenant and flushed between workloads under our tenancy policies. We can provide a control matrix and memory-scan report on request. (See Appendix §2.3, Evidence: control-mapping.xlsx)

3) RTO/RPO: Target SLOs: Dedicated: RTO for single-availability-instance failures is 5 minutes for failover to warm standby; RPO is <1 minute for stateful request replay (KV/prefix caches best-effort). Hosted: best-effort availability with zonal failover; we publish median latency and availability dashboards and can provide SLA commitments under Dedicated contracts. Operational playbooks are available for audit review.

--- End draft ---

Notes: for the RTO/RPO wording we should avoid hard guarantees for Hosted; keep SLA language limited to Dedicated and Private with references to contract schedule. Also confirm whether we can produce a memory-scan report by Friday — Vivek, can your team run that in the Staging Dedicated pool?

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups. Please find below our consolidated responses; I’ve attached a populated spreadsheet for row-by-row answers (seaboard_qna_response_table_v1.xlsx) and the appendix I shared earlier. Let us know if you want any answer softened or expanded for procurement/legal review.

--- Consolidated responses (summary) ---
1) Audit logs access: For Private (VPC) & Dedicated customers we support near-real-time streaming of audit events to customer destinations (TLS-secured SIEM forwarder) and scheduled exports (S3). Hosted customers have retained logs and can request scheduled exports; streaming is available as an add-on or as part of Dedicated.

Evidence available: sample logging exports, logging architecture diagram, ingestion configuration snippets (attached in appendix).

2) Cross-tenant memory / KV separation: Our runtime enforces tenant namespaces and per-tenant process isolation. Dedicated pools include isolated GPU allocation and process sandboxes; KV caches are namespaced and flushed on tenant boundary events. We can produce a memory-scan report for your scope after sign-off.

Evidence available: control matrix row mapping, memory-scan report (on request), tenancy architecture diagrams.

3) RTO / RPO targets: Dedicated: target RTO for single-instance failures is 5 minutes with warm standby failover. RPO target is under 1 minute for stateful replay where configured. Hosted: we publish performance/availability dashboards and can discuss contractual SLAs as part of Dedicated agreements.

Timeline commitments (if LOI signed): SOC2 excerpts + architecture diagrams: 5–7 business days. Memory-scan + control-mapping: 10 business days (may require a brief test window).

- We’ll upload the populated QnA spreadsheet to the shared drive (link below) and can schedule a 30-minute call with your security team tomorrow to walk through evidence artifacts.
